words: To say hello to someone when you meet them.
She greeted every guest at the door with a smile.
To tell someone another person's name when they meet for the first time.
Let me introduce my colleague, Ana.
A person who lives next to you or near you.
Our neighbour looks after our cat when we travel.
Saturday and Sunday, when many people do not work.
What did you do at the weekend?
An activity you enjoy doing in your free time.
My favourite hobby is cooking for friends.
To ask someone to come to an event or to your home.
They invited us to dinner on Saturday.
To say yes to an offer or an invitation.
I'd be happy to accept your invitation.
To say no politely to an offer or an invitation.
I'm afraid I have to decline — I'm busy that evening.
To do something enjoyable for a special occasion.
We went out to celebrate her new job.
To talk with someone you have not seen for a while about what has happened.
Let's meet for coffee and catch up next week.
To tell someone that something is good and they should try it.
Can you recommend a good restaurant near here?
I really appreciate your help with the move.
To say that you are sorry for something.
I apologise for being late this morning.
A polite thing to say when you meet someone for the first time.
Hi, I'm Tom. Nice to meet you.
An informal way to ask how someone is.
A friendly way to say goodbye.
Words you use to add something new to the conversation.
By the way, did you hear that Lisa is leaving?
In fact; used to correct something or add a surprising detail.
I thought it was hard, but actually it was easy.
I'll definitely come to your party.
An informal way to agree with a plan.
An informal way to say that something is not a problem.
Sorry I'm late. — No worries, we've just started.
What you say when someone has done something good or had good news.
What you say when you are sorry about bad news that is not serious.
You can't come? That's a shame.
To talk in a friendly, informal way.
We chatted about films for an hour.
To have a friendly relationship with someone.
I get on with everyone in my new team.
To decide what you are going to do and when.
Let's make plans for the summer holiday.
To go somewhere with other people or become a member of a group.
Would you like to join us for a walk?
A person you invite to your home or to an event.
We have three guests staying this weekend.
Something nice that you say about someone.
She paid me a compliment on my presentation.
Polite, light conversation about simple topics such as the weather.
Small talk about the weather is very common in Britain.
A piece of paper or a code that shows you have paid to travel or to enter.
I bought my train ticket on the app.
The place in a station where you get on and off a train.
The train to Leeds leaves from platform four.
The act of leaving, especially at the start of a journey.
Please arrive two hours before departure.
The act of reaching a place.
Our arrival time is half past six.
A time when something happens later than planned.
There is a delay of twenty minutes on this route.
To decide that something planned will not happen.
They cancelled the flight because of the storm.
To arrange to have a seat, room or table in the future.
I'd like to book a room for two nights.
An arrangement to keep a seat, room or table for you.
I have a reservation under the name Silva.
An official document you need to travel to other countries.
Don't forget your passport at the airport.
The bags and cases you take on a journey.
How much luggage can I take on the plane?
The document that lets you get on a plane.
Please show your boarding pass at the gate.
To arrive at a hotel or airport and say that you are there.
You can check in at the hotel from two o'clock.
To pay and leave a hotel.
We need to check out before eleven.
A ticket that lets you travel to a place and come back.
A return ticket to Brighton, please.
A list of times when trains, buses or classes happen.
Check the bus timetable before you leave.
A train, bus or plane that you change to during a journey.
I missed my connection in Paris.
The door at an airport where you get on your plane.
Flight 205 is now boarding at gate twelve.
A seat next to the passage between the rows, not by the window.
Could I have an aisle seat, please?
Instructions that tell you how to get to a place.
Can you give me directions to the museum?
To change direction to the left.
Turn left at the traffic lights.
Go straight on for about two hundred metres.
A place where two roads cross each other.
The hotel is just after the crossroads.
A round junction where cars go round in a circle.
Take the second exit at the roundabout.
The money you pay to travel on a bus, train or taxi.
The bus fare is two pounds fifty.
A place where taxis wait for passengers.
There's a taxi rank outside the station.
A place to stay, such as a hotel or flat.
Breakfast is included in the accommodation.
Visiting interesting places as a tourist.
We spent the morning sightseeing in the old town.
The act of travelling from one place to another.
The journey to work takes forty minutes.
A drawing of an area that shows roads and places.
Let me check the map on my phone.
Not knowing where you are or how to get somewhere.
Excuse me, I'm lost. Where is the station?
The amount of money you must pay for something.
The price of this jacket is forty pounds.
A reduction in the usual price.
Students get a ten percent discount.
A piece of paper that shows you have paid for something.
Keep the receipt in case you want to return it.
Money that is given back to you when you return something.
The shop gave me a full refund.
To give something back to a shop and take a different one.
Can I exchange these shoes for a bigger size?
Money in coins or notes, not a card.
Do you take cash or only card?
The money you get back when you pay more than the price.
Here's your change and your receipt.
A line of people waiting for something.
There was a long queue at the checkout.
How big or small something is, for example clothes.
Do you have this shirt in a smaller size?
To put on clothes to see if they fit or look good.
Can I try on this coat?
A small room in a shop where you try on clothes.
The fitting rooms are at the back of the shop.
Something you buy for less than its usual price.
Only five pounds? That's a bargain!
To have enough money to pay for something.
We can't afford a new car this year.
A plan for how much money you can spend.
I'm on a tight budget this month.
A document that shows how much you have to pay.
Could we have the bill, please?
Extra money you give to a waiter or driver to thank them.
We left a small tip for the waiter.
Available for less than the usual price.
These boots are on sale this week.
Not available in the shop at the moment.
Sorry, that model is out of stock.
The act of bringing goods to a person's home or office.
Delivery is free for orders over thirty pounds.
To ask for something to be brought or sent to you.
I ordered a new phone case online.
A way of paying by holding your card or phone near a machine.
You can pay contactless for anything under one hundred pounds.
To take money out of a bank account.
I need to withdraw some cash before the market.
The amount of money in a bank account.
I checked my balance on the banking app.
Restaurants in the city centre are expensive.
The market is a cheap place to buy fruit.
A question to ask the price of something.
This lamp is lovely. How much is it?
To look at things in a shop without a plan to buy.
A promise that a product will be repaired or replaced if it breaks.
The laptop comes with a two-year guarantee.
The place in a shop where you pay.
Please pay at the checkout by the door.
To say that you are not happy about something.
I complained because the food was cold.
An arranged time to see a doctor, dentist or another professional.
I have a doctor's appointment at ten.
A shop where you can buy medicine.
The pharmacy on the corner is open until eight.
A doctor's written order for a medicine.
The doctor gave me a prescription for antibiotics.
A sign that you are ill, such as a cough or a fever.
I've had a headache since this morning.
A pain in your throat, often when you have a cold.
I can't sing today — I've got a sore throat.
A body heat that is higher than normal, a sign of illness.
She has a temperature, so she's staying home.
To push air out of your throat with a sudden noise.
He has been coughing all night.
A bad reaction of the body to something, such as food or pollen.
I have an allergy to nuts.
Harm done to the body in an accident.
He missed the match because of a knee injury.
Take a painkiller and rest for a while.
To become healthy again after an illness.
It took me two weeks to recover from the flu.
A serious, dangerous situation that needs action immediately.
A vehicle that takes ill or injured people to hospital.
Someone called an ambulance after the accident.
A doctor who looks after teeth.
I go to the dentist twice a year.
A general medical examination to see if you are healthy.
I'm going for my yearly check-up.
Good for your body, or in good physical condition.
She eats a healthy breakfast every day.
Physical activity that keeps you fit.
I try to get some exercise every morning.
Worry caused by difficult situations or too much work.
Yoga helps me deal with stress.
The food that a person usually eats.
A good diet includes lots of vegetables.
To be less ill or less unhappy than before.
I hope you feel better soon.
What you say or write to someone who is ill.
Get well soon — we miss you at work.
Something you take to treat an illness.
Take this medicine twice a day.
The amount of a medicine you take at one time.
Don't take more than the recommended dose.
An unwanted effect of a medicine.
A common side effect is feeling tired.
To relax or sleep so your body can recover.
The doctor told me to rest for two days.
A document from a doctor saying you are too ill to work.
My manager asked for a sick note after five days.
A medical test of a small amount of your blood.
The nurse took a blood test this morning.
To hurt a joint, such as an ankle, by twisting it.
I sprained my ankle playing football.
Healthy and strong, especially because of exercise.
Cycling to work keeps me fit.
Money you pay regularly to live in a home that someone else owns.
The rent is due on the first of the month.
A person who owns a home and rents it to other people.
I called the landlord about the broken heating.
A home on one floor of a larger building.
We live in a two-bedroom flat.
Regular payments for things like electricity, water and internet.
Are the bills included in the rent?
A person who shares a house with you.
My housemate cooks dinner on Fridays.
I do the grocery shopping on Saturday morning.
Clothes that need to be washed, or the act of washing them.
I need to do the laundry tonight.
To collect used things so they can be used again.
We recycle all our glass and paper.
To travel regularly between home and work.
I commute to the city by train.
A short trip to do a job, such as buying something.
I have a few errands to run after work.
Regular jobs at home, such as cleaning and washing up.
We share the chores between us.
The usual order in which you do things.
Walking the dog is part of my morning routine.
Food that was not eaten at a meal and is kept for later.
We had the leftovers for lunch the next day.
A cold box in the kitchen where food is kept.
There's some milk in the fridge.
Not working because it has been damaged.
The washing machine is broken again.
To fix something that is broken.
A technician is coming to repair the boiler.
A person whose job is to fit and repair water pipes.
We need a plumber — the kitchen tap is leaking.
A hole or crack that lets water or gas escape.
There's a leak under the sink.
A secret word or code you use to open an account or a network.
Something wrapped in paper or a box, sent by post.
A parcel arrived for you this morning.
A place where you can send letters and parcels.
I need to go to the post office to send this.
Please put the empty bottles in the green bin.
To make a place clean and in order.
Let's tidy up before the guests arrive.
To take something from someone and give it back later.
To give something to someone for a short time.
Could you lend me ten pounds until Friday?
Money you pay at the start of renting a home, returned at the end.
We got our deposit back when we moved out.
It's a quiet neighbourhood with a nice park.
The system that keeps a building warm.
Can you turn the heating up a little?
To leave your home and go to live in a new one.
To carry the rubbish from the house to the bin outside.
It's your turn to take out the rubbish.
